name: SWT-Bench
description: A benchmark where models are given real GitHub issue descriptions and must generate unit tests that reproduce the reported bug — specifically, tests that fail on the original codebase and pass after the canonical patch is applied. Derived from the same 12 Python repositories as SWE-bench, but inverts the task: instead of generating a patch, the model generates the test suite. Measures both reproduction success rate and line-coverage increase on the resolving patch.
evaluation_method: success rate (tests fail before patch, pass after); coverage increase (ΔC) on resolving patch
general_score_metric: success rate 𝒮 (% of issues reproduced); coverage increase ΔC
typical_sota_score: ~87% success on Verified (TEX-T by Salesforce, 2025); frontier models score 50–87% on Verified; baseline agents score ~18% on Lite
reputation: NeurIPS 2024; from ETH Zurich SRI Lab; introduces the complementary task to SWE-bench (test generation vs. patch generation); official leaderboard at swtbench.com; used alongside SWE-bench to evaluate full bug-fix validation pipelines
notes: NeurIPS 2024. Full split contains 1,983 instances after filtering from 2,294 original (same repos as SWE-bench). BM25 retrieval provides 27k-token context window (cl100k_base). Two prompt formats: ZeroShotBase (zsb) and ZeroShotPlus (zsp). SWT-bench Lite (276 instances) and SWT-bench Verified (433 instances) are focused subsets. Official leaderboard: swtbench.com. arXiv: 2406.12952.

institutions: ETH Zurich (SRI Lab — Secure, Reliable, and Intelligent Systems Lab)
